== Katherine Glasgow, wife of Thomas Weir: testament dative and inventory ==

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; background:#f8fff8; border:2px solid #8DB600;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Genealogical result
|-
| '''[[Glasgow-1495|Katherine Glasgow]] was the wife of [[Weir-4172|Thomas Weir]] in Stevenston parish.''' She died in '''January 1603'''. Thomas submitted her estate account in the names of '''William, James and probably Jonet—Janet—Weir''', the executors-dative. The confirmation expressly refers to the executors' '''minority'''. They were therefore very probably Katherine and Thomas's children, although the surviving wording does not expressly call them sons, daughter or ''bairns''.
|}

This page is a working transcription and modern-English rendering of the Glasgow Commissary Court testament dative and inventory of Katherine Glasgow, National Records of Scotland '''CC9/7/4, images 6–7'''.<ref name="Original">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/4, images 6–7, testament dative and inventory of Katherine Glasgow; original register images accessed through [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People, wills and testaments].</ref> It is not a complete diplomatic edition: unresolved words and sums remain marked rather than reconstructed from formula.

Katherine's entry begins at the '''bottom of image 6''', after the preceding testament, and continues through most of image 7. A different person's testament begins at the bottom of image 7. Text outside those boundaries does not belong to Katherine's estate.

The document is a '''testament dative'''—a court-appointed administration and inventory—not a personal will stating Katherine's wishes.<ref name="Dative">Scotland's People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/guides/wills-and-testaments “Wills and testaments”], explanation of testaments dative and testamentar.</ref>

The significant wording is approximately:

: … be the said '''Thomas Weir hir spous''', In name [and behalf?] of '''William, James and [Jonet?] Weiris, executouris dativeis decernit''' …

and, in the confirmation:

: … in respect of the '''executouris dativis minoritie''' …

Minor children were the natural people for a surviving husband to represent in their mother's intestate estate. The combination of shared surname, Thomas acting for them and their minority makes the child relationship strong. Nevertheless, executor status alone is not an explicit kin term, so the profile relationship should be labelled '''probable/uncertain''' unless another record supplies it directly.

The manuscript confirmation day appears to be '''[26?] May 1605'''. Francis J. Grant's printed calendar and the Findmypast transcript both give '''9 May 1605'''.<ref name="Calendar">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196], “Glasgow, Katherine, spouse to Thomas Weir, par. of Steinstone 9 May 1605”; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FWILLS%2F057453&tab=this Findmypast transcript SCOT/WILLS/057453].</ref> Until the numeral is independently resolved, '''May 1605''' is secure and the exact confirmation day should remain disputed. Neither candidate date is a marriage date.

== Working transcription ==

Abbreviations are expanded where reasonably clear and punctuation is supplied. '''[…]''' marks unresolved text; '''[word?]''' marks a tentative reading; '''[sum]''' marks a figure not securely read.

=== Opening: bottom of image 6 to top of image 7 ===

<blockquote>
The Testament dative and Inventar of the<br/>
guidis, geir, debtis and sowmes of money quhilkis pertenit to<br/>
umquhile '''Cathereine Glasgow, spous to Thomas Weir''', in the<br/>
parochyn of '''Stevinsoune''', quha deceist in the<br/>
moneth of '''Januar 1603''' ȝeiris, faithfullie maid and gevin<br/>
up be the said '''Thomas Weir hir spous''', In name [and behalf?]<br/>
of '''William, James and [Jonet?] Weiris, executouris dativeis decernit'''<br/>
<br/>
[Image 7]<br/>
to hir guidis and geir be decreit of the Commissar of Glasgow […]<br/>
the […] day of Apryle lastbypast, as the decreit thairupone<br/>
beiris.
</blockquote>

The collective surname ''Weiris'' applies to all three forenames. ''Jonet'' is the preferred reading of the third, but is less secure than William and James.

=== Inventory ===

<blockquote>
'''Inventar'''<br/>
<br/>
Item, the said umquhile Cathereine had in hir possessioun the tyme<br/>
of hir deceis foirsaid the guidis and geir following, of the availl<br/>
eftermentionat, viz.: '''Twa gray hors''', price thame [sum]. Item,<br/>
'''ane auld blak naig''', price thairof [sum]. Item, '''twa kye''', the<br/>
price of the peice [sum], Summa [sum]. Item, '''ane forrow kow''',<br/>
price [sum]. Item, in '''beir''' […] bollis and […] firlotis, price<br/>
of the boll with the fodder [sum], Summa [sum].<br/>
Item, […] '''aitis''', at the boll with the fodder [sum],<br/>
Summa [sum]. Item, the '''insicht of hir hous, with the abulȝement<br/>
of hir body''', estimat worth [sum].<br/>
<br/>
Summa of the Inventar foirsaid — [sum].<br/>
<br/>
'''Na debtis awand In.'''
</blockquote>

The estate contained two grey horses, an old black nag, two cows, a farrow cow, bere or barley, oats and fodder, household contents and Katherine's clothing. A ''farrow'' cow was one which had not calved that season; the word does not necessarily mean that it gave no milk.<ref>Dictionaries of the Scots Language, [https://dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/farrow “farrow”].</ref> No debts owed to Katherine were recorded.

=== Debts owed by Katherine ===

<blockquote>
'''Debttis awand Out'''<br/>
<br/>
Item, awand be hir to '''James erle of Glencairne, hir maister''',<br/>
of mailles the said 1603 ȝeiris, [sum]. Item, to '''Mr Alex[ande]r Campbel,<br/>
minister at Stevinsoune''', of teynd corne the said ȝeir, vj bollis,<br/>
price of the boll [sum], Summa [sum]. Item, to '''[Bryce?]<br/>
Blair of [Lochwod?]''', [sum]. Item, to '''Archebald [Muir?]''',<br/>
[…] [sum]. Item, to '''Johnne Weir in nether [place-name unclear]''',<br/>
[sum]. Item, to '''Johnne [Wicht?], hir servand''', of fie the said<br/>
ȝeir, [sum]. Item, to '''[Jeane Doun?], hir uther servand''', the said<br/>
ȝeir of fie, [sum].<br/>
<br/>
Summa of the debttis Out — [sum].<br/>
<br/>
'''Et sic debita excedunt bona.'''<br/>
<br/>
[In the margin:] '''Quota nulla.'''
</blockquote>

The Latin means, “And thus the debts exceed the assets.” ''Quota nulla'' records that no confirmation quota was due. The liabilities place the household within the Glencairn estate and Stevenston parish economy: rent was owed to James, Earl of Glencairn; teind grain to the parish minister; other private debts and two servants' unpaid wages were also recorded. The uncertain personal names should not be used as firm identities.

=== Confirmation ===

<blockquote>
At Glasgow the '''[xxvj?] day of Maij 1605''' ȝeiris, I '''Robert<br/>
Chirnsyde of Over Possill, Commissar of Glasgow''', constitut be our<br/>
Soverane Lord, eftir dew warning maid be edict oppinly as<br/>
effeirit, Be the tennour heirof ratifeis, approvis and confirmis<br/>
this present testament and inventar, in sa far as the samyn is<br/>
dewlie and trewlie gevin up, etc. And gevis and committis full<br/>
power and intromissioun with the guidis and geir abonewrittin<br/>
to the saidis executouris dativis abonespecifeit allanerlie, with power to<br/>
thame to call and persew thairfoir. [Ordanis?] the upgivar<br/>
to mak faith as use is, in respect of the '''executouris dativis minori-<br/>
tie'''. And hes fund '''Johnne Craufurd in Glen'''<br/>
cautioun that the guidis and geir salbe furthcumand to all […]<br/>
[…] entres as law will. And the upgivar become actit<br/>
to releif his said cautioun of the premissis.
</blockquote>

Robert Chirnsyde of Over Possill approved the administration after public notice and granted the executors authority over the estate. Because the executors were minors, Thomas, as the person submitting the inventory, made the customary oath on their behalf. John Crawford in Glen acted as cautioner or surety; neither man is identified as kin.

John Weir is worth pursuing because his surname and locality may connect him to Thomas or the minor executors. The debt entry alone proves only a financial association.

== Modern-English summary ==

[[Glasgow-1495|Katherine Glasgow]], wife of [[Weir-4172|Thomas Weir]] in Stevenston parish, died in January 1603. Thomas submitted the inventory for William, James and probably Janet Weir, who had been appointed executors-dative. The court later described the executors collectively as minors. That pattern makes them very probably the couple's children, although the document does not expressly say so.

Katherine's estate comprised horses, cattle, grain, fodder, household goods and clothing. No money was recorded as owed to her. Her liabilities—rent, teind grain, private debts and servants' wages—exceeded the estate's assets.

The testament was confirmed in May 1605 by Robert Chirnsyde of Over Possill. The manuscript day appears to be [26?], while the published calendar and Findmypast index give 9 May; the exact day remains unresolved. John Crawford in Glen guaranteed the administration.

Fully paged WikiTree searches completed on 8 September 2026, including the principal historical spellings of Weir and each given name, found no compatible existing profile for William, James or Jonet/Janet. Each is therefore a separate profile-creation candidate. Their links to Thomas and Katherine, estimated birth ranges and inferred Stevenston birthplaces must remain uncertain; Jonet's forename is also provisional.

== Research priorities ==

# Search Stevenston parish, Glencairn estate and commissary records for William, James and Jonet/Janet Weir with Thomas Weir, Katherine Glasgow or the same locality. The profile duplicate audit is complete; the remaining target is an explicit parentage, tutory, marriage or inheritance record that could upgrade the probable child relationships.
# Reinspect the confirmation numeral and compare it with other dates written by the same clerk; reconcile the manuscript with the 9 May printed calendar.
# Resolve John Weir's ''Nether …'' residence and test whether he appears with Thomas or the three minor executors elsewhere.
# Keep Katherine's possible relationship to the Corsinkell Glasgows and to [[Glasgow-3179|Geillis Glasgow]] as a locality-network hypothesis. This testament names no parent or sibling.
